name: MonarchButtonGroup
title: ButtonGroup
summary: Related buttons shown as one control: joined into one shape with square inner corners, or kept apart with a small gap, with one variant and size for all of them.
whenToUse: For two to five closely related actions that belong together, such as Previous and Next, Day, Week and Month, or zoom in and out.
whenNotToUse: For one choice out of several that stays selected use segmented buttons (SingleChoiceSegmentedButtonRow) or MonarchRadioRow. For options that stay on or off use the toggles in ToggleButton. For a single action use MonarchButton.
api: @Composable fun MonarchButtonGroup(modifier: Modifier = Modifier, orientation: Orientation = Orientation.Horizontal, variant: MonarchButtonVariant = MonarchButtonVariant.Secondary, size: MonarchButtonSize = MonarchButtonSize.Md, attached: Boolean = true, fullWidth: Boolean = false, label: String? = null, content: MonarchButtonGroupScope.() -> Unit)

interface MonarchButtonGroupScope { fun button(text: String, onClick: () -> Unit, enabled: Boolean = true, leadingIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null); fun iconButton(contentDescription: String, onClick: () -> Unit, enabled: Boolean = true, icon: @Composable () -> Unit) }

options.name: variant
options.description: Primary, Secondary, Ghost or Danger, for every button.

options.name: size
options.description: Sm, Md or Lg: the visible height of every button in a row. In a column every button is at least 48dp high.

options.name: attached
options.description: Joins the buttons into one shape. When false they keep an 8dp gap.

options.name: fullWidth
options.description: Fills the available width. In a row the buttons share it equally.

options.name: label
options.description: What the buttons have in common, read by TalkBack. Already localised.

options.name: content
options.description: Declares the buttons in order with button(text, onClick, enabled, leadingIcon) and iconButton(contentDescription, onClick, enabled, icon).

states.name: resting
states.description: One shape with rounded outer corners. Secondary buttons share one 1dp border between neighbours; the other variants are separated by a 1dp gap.

states.name: pressed
states.description: Only the pressed button shows the Material ripple.

states.name: disabled
states.description: A button declared with enabled = false takes the disabled fill and text color of its variant and ignores taps; the others are unchanged.

states.name: focused
states.description: The focused button draws the Monarch focus ring around its own shape.

states.name: not attached
states.description: Each button is drawn alone with full corners and an 8dp gap.

appearance: Every button uses the colors of its MonarchButton variant: accent solid for Primary, the surface with the default border for Secondary, no fill for Ghost and danger solid for Danger, with the disabled roles when disabled. The outer corners are 8dp. The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web group joins any child and lets each child keep its own variant; here, as on iOS, the group sets one variant and size for all its buttons. A Compose container cannot restyle a MonarchButton passed to it, so the buttons are declared through MonarchButtonGroupScope (as items are declared in a LazyColumn) and drawn by the group with Material 3 Buttons and the MonarchButton tokens. Material 3 1.4 has a ButtonGroup and connected button shapes only as experimental expressive APIs, so they are not used. In a row each button is drawn at its size inside a 48dp touch target, and all buttons take the height of the tallest one, found from their intrinsic heights. In a column every button is at least 48dp high because the buttons touch.
accessibility: The group is a traversal group, and with a label its content description is the label, so TalkBack reads it before the buttons.
Every button stays its own element with the Button role, its own click action and its own enabled state.
An icon button is named by its contentDescription; its icon is given a null description.
Every button reserves a touch target of at least 48dp by 48dp, in a row and in a column.
Labels wrap instead of being cut off at font scale 2.0, and the other buttons in the row grow to the same height.
The first button is at the start in both layout directions, and the rounded corners follow it.
A focused button draws the Monarch focus ring.
edgeCases: One button gives a single shape with all corners rounded. A group with no buttons draws nothing.
With fullWidth in a row, a long label wraps inside its equal share of the width.
Attached secondary buttons overlap by 1dp so that neighbours share one border line.
The label is optional; without one the buttons are read without a group name.
